'''Nova crystals''' were a valuable and highly sought after [[gemstone]], admired for their rarity, beauty, and industrial applications throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="GSWU" /><ref name="KILO" /><ref name="CSWE" />

==Properties==
Nova crystals were bluish-white gemstones that possessed the unusual property of amplifying light,<ref name="SWTOR" /><ref name="GSWU" /> glowing with an inner luminescence as a result,<ref name="CSWE" /> characterized by a glimmering prismatic sparkle.<ref name="KILO" />

Key to the Nova crystal was its unique crystalline matrix; this matrix, when exposed to bright sunlight (especially in the red color band), absorbed heat from ambient light and became excited energetically. This created the Nova crystal's signature glow, which was often bright enough to be its own light source.<ref name="CSWE" /> Mining Nova crystals was risky and dangerous business, however; when removed from its rocky matrix and exposed to temperatures over thirty degrees celsius, a raw nova crystal became increasing unstable and prone to spontaneous reaction to the slightest jarring. Such raw crystals were highly explosive,<ref name="KILO" /> and capable of exploding with incredible force,<ref name="CSWE" /> with even a single small flake capable of completely destroying a [[A-A6z Speeder Truck]]. Raw crystals thus have to be refrigerated for transport, where they are then taken to industrial worlds where they can be bonded to inert trace elements that stabilize the crystalline matrices.<ref name="KILO" />

==Applications==
Nova crystals were a valuable gemstone used as currency on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]],<ref name="SWGB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> and were commonly crafted into valuable jewelry.<ref name="GSWU" /><ref name="SMOKE" /> Additionally, due to their ability to amplify light, Nova crystals had numerous applications in optoelectronics, being used in the construction of [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] and [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]].<ref name="GSWU" /> Less commonly, raw crystals could be used as explosive devices.

==History==
Nova crystals notably helped bankroll the first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] project for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]] held immense deposits of nova crystals, which contributed greatly to its reputation for [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]] wealth.<ref name="CSWE" /> Nova crystals made up the primary industry of the planet [[Cotellier/Legends|Cotellier]], but the world was remote enough to be harassed by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] regularly, and never rose to the fame of [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]]. Sizable Nova crystal deposits were extremely rare, and were significant enough that their discovery had huge economic implications; when Nova crystal veins were found on [[Krann]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] subjugated the entire planet and enslaved the native [[Kluuzot]] to harvest the crystals.<ref name="KILO" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Novamine.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An example of green Nova crystals in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'']]
There seems to be a discrepancy in the color of Nova crystals; Nova crystals were first described as bluish-white with a luminescence in 1984's ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'' first edition, which expanded on the 1979 ''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]'' (which itself mentioned, but did not describe Nova crystals). This was upheld by [[Twin Stars of Kira (sourcebook)|''Twin Stars of Kira'']] in 1993, which described Nova crystals as sparkling and prismatic.

It wasn't until 2001 in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' that Nova crystals were portrayed as green; in the game they are found on virtually every world, and are used to fund research for advanced technologies and pay for troops and vehicles. Nova crystals have not been green since this game, excluding a singular special [[Rare Nova Crystal|instance]] in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''. Indeed, the later ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' seems to fix this issue, by showing the Nova crystal as a bluish-white crystal with an inner luminescence, which is in line with the [[Nova crystal|new canon version]].
